q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEWER_ID , VIEW_DATE , COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS COUNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID , VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ) A ORDER BY VIEWER_ID ASC
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEWER_ID , VIEW_DATE , COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS COUNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID , VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ) A ORDER BY VIEWER_ID ASC
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (3, 103, 201, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE. This difference in grouping affects the results when there are multiple view dates for the same viewer_id.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have multiple view dates for the same viewer_id, and the count of distinct article_ids should be greater than 1 for at least one of the view dates.
